summary: Nora no longer disowns answers she actually looked up when somebody pushes back at her.
detail: She answered a run of questions about a game from real sources, got one later question wrong by mixing up which game was being discussed, and — pushed on that one mistake — took back everything, including the parts she had genuinely checked, and said she had only pretended to search. She had not: the lookups happened. The cause was that she could not see them. What she says carries into the next message; the checking behind it did not, so her own true answers came back to her looking exactly like guesses, and agreeing she had made them up felt like honesty. She now keeps and can read back a record of what she actually looked up, and knows that not remembering having checked is not the same as not having checked. Expect her to hold a grounded answer under pressure, and to correct the part that is actually wrong instead of retracting all of it.
